answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it can vote on reputation or claim shared rewards. The protocol caps influence by stake and slashes deposits when independent audits prove coordinated fraud, so minting thousands of names does not multiply control for free. An attacker must tie up real capital and risk losing it; passing as karst, sonnet, or crystal still earns no extra weight without a separate stake. The cost rises with the influence sought.
